title: The porcupine dilemma
idea: Close to others we get warmth, but also pricked by their sharp edges. The answer is a distance where you can bear each other.
apply: If a relationship keeps getting prickly, change the dose: shorter visits and more space, then more warmth.
remind: Stay close enough for warmth, far enough to avoid the spikes.
who: Elena, who loves her sister but clashes with her on long visits.

scenes.cap: is when Elena and her sister start to clash
scenes.sub: They love each other. That is the puzzle.
scenes.nar: Elena loves her sister Mara, but after three days together, they start to clash.
Schopenhauer imagined porcupines in winter. Huddled too close, they prick each other. Too far apart, they freeze.
Like the porcupines, they find a distance they can both bear. A weekly call, visits that last two days, and time apart afterward.
The fights fade, and both look forward to visits. The warmth lasts because neither keeps getting pricked.
